steps.name: QC diagnostics and outlier characterization
caveats: Duplication rate is reported at the library QC level, not computable from gene counts alone — treat it as an external caveat to correlate against group and library size, not something to recompute from the counts file
Do not attempt to deduplicate or renormalize counts to 'correct' duplication — for non-UMI rRNA-depleted libraries this is not standard and can worsen DE inference per published evidence
steps.question: Given the counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 treated vs 6 control) and metadata.csv, how do library size, sample correlation/PCA structure, and the reported high duplication rate relate to the treatment groups, and how much of an outlier is sample_01 (library size ~4x below median)?
acceptance_criteria: Reports per-sample library size (total counts) for all 12 samples and flags sample_01 quantitatively (fold-difference from median)
Produces a sample-sample correlation heatmap and a PCA plot colored by treated/control group to check whether sample_01 and/or duplication-related effects separate from the treatment axis

States explicitly whether the high duplication rate appears confounded with treatment group (e.g. by comparing group-wise library size distributions) since QC-only artifacts should not be corrected via deduplication per literature evidence (Parekh et al. 2016) for non-UMI data

Produces a written recommendation on whether sample_01 should be excluded, downweighted, or retained for the DE step, with justification tied to observed leverage/outlier diagnostics (e.g. Cook's distance proxy or PCA distance)

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control (primary + sample_01 sensitivity)
caveats: n=6 per group is modest power; do not overclaim significance for genes near the threshold
Unpaired single-batch design means no batch correction is needed, but confirm metadata truly contains only the two-level condition column before building the design formula

Only 12000 genes total (already filtered gene-level count matrix) — apply DESeq2's built-in independent filtering but check it is not removing an excessive fraction given the smaller-than-genome-wide feature set
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) heart samples, and how sensitive are the results to inclusion/exclusion of the low-library-size sample_01 identified in QC?
acceptance_criteria: Runs DESeq2 (Wald test, treated vs control, single-batch unpaired design ~condition) on raw integer gene-level counts with default size-factor normalization

Reports full DE table (log2FC, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value/padj) for all genes, with genes called significant at padj < 0.05 (or explicitly stated alternate threshold if independent filtering removes too many genes given only 12000 features)
Repeats the DESeq2 run excluding sample_01 as a sensitivity analysis and reports the overlap of significant gene sets between the full-cohort and sample_01-excluded runs
Reports diagnostic plots: dispersion estimates, MA plot, and a volcano plot of the primary (all-sample) result
States final recommended DE gene list, explicitly flagging whether conclusions depend materially on sample_01's inclusion

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated vs control signature
caveats: Gene sets use HGNC gene symbols — confirm the counts.csv gene symbol column matches this identifier space directly; if not, use the human UniProt ID mapping or NCBI human gene_info reference to reconcile symbols before enrichment
WikiPathways gmt here is a general human pathway snapshot, not heart-specific — report enrichment findings as descriptive, not confirmatory, of cardiac mechanism
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control heart samples?
acceptance_criteria: Runs over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment (fgsea or clusterProfiler) on the DESeq2 result from T1S2 using both the WikiPathways human gene sets and the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets available in the environment
Uses the full ranked gene list (e.g. by signed -log10(p) x sign(log2FC) or Wald statistic) for GSEA rather than only the padj<0.05 subset, to retain statistical power given n=6 per group
Reports enriched terms with adjusted p-values (BH/FDR) and effect direction (up in treated vs up in control)
Cross-references results from T1S2's sample_01-sensitivity analysis: notes if top enriched pathways change materially when sample_01 is excluded

plan.title: Heart treated vs control DE with duplication/outlier QC
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a bulk RNA-seq dataset (12000 genes x 13 columns, 12 samples: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs) with raw Salmon gene-level counts. Two QC caveats directly affect the design: (1) duplication rate >60% in most libraries — expected for rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs, and literature (Parekh et al. 2016, Sci Rep) shows that computational deduplication on non-UMI data does not improve and can worsen DE power/FDR, so counts should NOT be deduplicated post-hoc; duplication is instead documented as a QC caveat and checked for correlation with library size/PC structure so it is not confounded with treatment. (2) sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which can distort size-factor normalization and inflate its leverage on dispersion estimation — this requires an explicit QC decision (flag, and either downweight or exclude with justification) rather than silent inclusion. The plan therefore runs: QC/exploratory diagnostics (library size, duplication proxy via count distribution, PCA/sample correlation) to characterize the outlier and its impact; a DESeq2 (or edgeR as cross-check) differential expression step comparing treated vs control that reports results run both with and without sample_01 to quantify its influence; and a downstream pathway enrichment step on the resulting DE gene list using WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, restricted to genes annotated in the count matrix, to interpret the treated-vs-control signature biologically. Only 12000 genes and 12 samples are involved, so all steps are lightweight computationally.
